annotations.text:
EduAI — four directions for the same screen.

Same content every time: the hero, the pricing rule (50% first month / 10% after), and three real tutor listings. Only the visual language changes, so you're comparing directions rather than layouts.

Pick one and I'll build it through all 30 templates.

A · MATRA — structure borrowed from Bengali script, where letters hang from a horizontal headline stroke. Every block hangs from a rule; no cards, no shadows, no rounded corners. Indigo and turmeric.

Why: rooted in Bangladesh without resorting to flag colours.
Tradeoff: austere. Lives or dies on typography being right.

B · LEDGER — the product is really months booked and taka settled, so it reads like a register. Mono numerals, ruled rows, one green signal colour, zero decoration.

Why: honest about what the app does; ages well; very fast to scan.
Tradeoff: cool and transactional — weak at persuading a first-time visitor.

C · SLATE — the classroom as material: dark slate ground, warm chalk-gold accent, editorial serif headlines.

Why: the only warm, human option here; photographs and faces would sit well on it.
Tradeoff: dark UI is harder work across dense admin tables and long forms.

D · BAZAAR — takes its cue from Bangladeshi street print and signage: heavy display type, flat colour blocks, thick black rules, no gradients.

Why: the most memorable of the four; unmistakably not a template.
Tradeoff: loud. Needs discipline to stay readable across admin screens.
